state.spec_5_1: Class precedence is absolute: override > task > witness. An override outranks a task, a task outranks a witness, EVEN WHEN THE WITNESS IS A DESCENDANT OF THE TASK.
state.spec_5_2: Per-key resolution, streaming model. Step 2: compare the candidate's class to the current setter's class using class precedence. Step 3: IF R's class is EQUAL, then R is a descendant of the current setter iff R is reachable from the current setter via the parent chain; if so R wins, if not the current setter wins.
state.q: An override record is an ANCESTOR of a task record and both set the same key. Which one sets the final value?

state.spec_5_5: An orphan is a record with a parent id that is not present. The record is excluded from the fold. An orphan's DESCENDANTS ARE NOT AUTO-ORPHANED: being descended from an orphan does not by itself make a record an orphan.
state.q: A record K descends from an orphan O. K is not itself an orphan. Do K's own effects enter the final state?

state.spec_1_1: The id field: 'The unique identifier. Must be free of \n and : (the closure root format uses these as delimiters).'
state.spec_1_1_malformed: A record missing any of id, parents, kind, effects, reason is malformed; the fold excludes malformed records from the applied set.
state.q: A record's id is 'a:b' -- it contains a colon, which section 1.1 says the id must be free of. Is that record malformed and excluded from the fold?

state.spec_1_1: The kind field: 'One of task, witness, override. Other values are accepted; their semantics are out of scope for the fold.' kind is optional, defaulting to null.
state.spec_5_1: Class precedence is absolute: override > task > witness.
state.spec_5_2: Per-key resolution compares the candidate's class to the current setter's class. Every record that sets a key is a candidate.
state.q: A record has kind: null and sets a key that an override record also sets. What class does the null-kind record have, and which one wins?
